summary: REJECT. Four quality gates fail on genuine, non-infrastructure grounds: (1) cargo fmt --all --check exits 1 across 93 files / 13 crates; (2) cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 101 with 4 real lint violations; (3) cargo test --workspace exits 101 with 2 failing tests (rustls crypto-provider feature-unification); (4) the 250 pure-LOC module ceiling is violated by 20 production library modules (worst: policy-rollout/src/state_machine.rs at 1304). SPDX presence and bench-schema gates PASS. Missing privileged/external infrastructure (BPF load, PostgreSQL, SPIRE, OIDC) is NOT counted against per task guidance. A nix-toolchain clippy defect (E0514 serde SVH) is documented as a toolchain issue, separate from the real clippy lint findings revealed by the rustup toolchain.

cargo_fmt.root_cause: rustfmt.toml declares nightly-only options (format_strings, group_imports, import_granularity, wrap_comments, format_code_in_doc_comments, normalize_comments, match_arm_bodies, condense_wildcard_suffixes) that the pinned stable toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml channel=1.95.0) IGNORES with warnings. The committed code was formatted with nightly rustfmt honoring those options; stable rustfmt applies different line-wrapping heuristics and reformats 93 files. The repo's own README claims 'cargo fmt --all --check -> exit 0' but that was recorded at task 1 when no Rust source existed.
cargo_fmt.notes: Genuine gate failure on the pinned stable toolchain. Resolution requires either (a) reformatting the workspace with stable rustfmt (cargo fmt --all) and removing/feature-gating the nightly-only rustfmt.toml options, or (b) moving the fmt gate to a nightly toolchain. Either is a PR-tracked decision.

cargo_clippy.notes: clippy aborts on the first error batch per crate, so additional violations may exist in crates not reached after the abort. TOOLCHAIN DEFECT (separate from the lint findings above): the default nix-profile toolchain in PATH (rustc 1.95.0 59807616e 'built from a source tarball', LLVM 21.1.8) fails clippy with error[E0514] 'found crate serde compiled by an incompatible version of rustc' on a CLEAN build, masking all lint results. This E0514 reproduces on both the nix toolchain and via `rustup run`; it was bypassed only by placing the rustup toolchain bin (LLVM 22.1.2) first in PATH with an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR. The code itself compiles cleanly: `cargo test --workspace` builds the same serde-heavy workspace (incl. protocol) with 0 E0514. The E0514 is a clippy-driver/serde-1.0.229 (serde_core) SVH incompatibility under this rustc, classified as a toolchain/infrastructure defect, NOT a code defect.

cargo_test.root_cause: rustls 0.23 crypto-provider feature-unification ambiguity. crates/identity-spiffe/Cargo.toml declares rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", ...] } (ring only). Under `cargo test --workspace`, cargo unifies features across the workspace and a transitive dependency enables rustls's aws-lc-rs default feature, so BOTH providers are enabled and CryptoProvider::get_default() panics (it requires exactly one). Per-crate runs pass (learnings: `cargo test -p identity-spiffe` = 82 tests) because only ring is enabled in isolation.
cargo_test.notes: Genuine workspace-integration failure, independent of toolchain (reproduces on both nix and rustup toolchains). Fix options: (a) call rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider().install_default() before building TLS configs in credentials.rs, or (b) align rustls feature selection workspace-wide so only one provider is enabled. The remaining 705 tests pass.

loc_check.task_exemptions_applied: test files (15) and generated code exempt per task; vmlinux.h is a generated BTF header (not flagged, git-untracked); release/out/.scaffold-work/*.c are gitignored build artifacts (exempt).
loc_check.notes: Genuine failure. The plan's 250 pure-LOC module ceiling (clippy.toml too-many-lines-threshold=250, scripts/loc-lint.sh) is violated by 20 production library modules + 3 binaries/build scripts, plus 7 BPF C/H files and 6 scripts under the repo's broader loc-lint scan. Most egregious: policy-rollout/src/state_machine.rs at 1304 pure-LOC (5.2x the ceiling). Only 2 files are baselined waivers. BPF C sensors are inherently large (512-byte stack, no dynamic allocation, inlined CO-RE) but still trip the repo's own gate.

presence_check.notes: Every committed .rs file (223) and every committed .bpf.c file (8 under bpf/sensors/) carries an SPDX-License-Identifier. BPF sensors that load into the kernel use GPL-2.0-only (LSM-compatible per README policy); placeholder.bpf.c and event_abi.h use (MIT OR Apache-2.0); Rust uses Apache-2.0 OR MIT. The 2 .c files under release/out/.scaffold-work/ that lack SPDX are gitignored build artifacts (.gitignore:62 'release/out/', regenerated by release-verify.sh; 0 tracked) and are exempt. vmlinux.h is a generated BTF header (.h, out of the .rs/.c scope).

repo_value_gate.root_cause: Tooling/allowlist string-mismatch, NOT a licensing-policy violation. spdx-lint.sh's RELAXED_LICENSE_ALLOWLIST lists the literal string 'Dual MIT/Apache-2.0', but the two files use the standard SPDX expression '(MIT OR Apache-2.0)'. The string comparison fails even though both files ARE correctly dual-licensed MIT/Apache (which the policy permits for non-LSM tracing programs and headers). Fix: add '(MIT OR Apache-2.0)' and 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT' to the RELAXED allowlist (the Rust files use 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT', a third ordering).
repo_value_gate.notes: The task's literal SPDX gate (presence of SPDX-License-Identifier on .rs/.c) PASSES. The repo's stricter value-based gate fails on a technicality; documented as a tooling finding.

bench_schemas.notes: All 6 versioned bench schemas exist. No numeric drift detected between the plan and the bench schemas.

genuine_production_logic_findings.assessment: Bare .unwrap() in DFS cycle detection (dfs_cycle). Logically infallible given the gray-node invariant (a color==1 node is always on the current DFS stack), but the unwrap relies on algorithm bookkeeping correctness and would panic if that invariant broke. Recommend .expect("gray node must be on DFS stack") or handling None.

unwrap_panic_check.notes: No dangerous production-runtime panic on user/runtime data was found. The single genuine production-logic bare unwrap (rules/lists.rs:109) is invariant-guarded and minor. The bulk of the 86 grep hits are idiomatic metric-registration expects, hyper response builders with static headers, mock/test-support structs living in src/, and dev/CLI binaries. Reported as a qualified finding rather than a hard failure, but the literal gate ('no production-code unwrap/panic') is not clean.

toolchain_findings: nix-profile rustc 1.95.0 (59807616e, 'built from a source tarball', LLVM 21.1.8) fails `cargo clippy` with E0514 (serde/serde_core SVH incompatibility) on clean builds, masking lint results. The rustup 1.95.0 toolchain (LLVM 22.1.2) runs clippy correctly. Both report the same rustc version string, so the E0514 is a build/SVH defect, not a version drift. Recommend standardizing on one consistent toolchain for CI.
rustfmt.toml nightly-only options are ignored on the pinned stable toolchain, causing the workspace-wide cargo fmt failure (93 files). Reconcile the formatter toolchain with rustfmt.toml.

spdx-lint.sh RELAXED allowlist does not recognize standard SPDX dual-license syntax '(MIT OR Apache-2.0)' / 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT' (only the literal 'Dual MIT/Apache-2.0'), producing 2 false-positive violations.
notes: Verdict REJECT is driven by four genuine, non-infrastructure gate failures: cargo fmt (93 files / 13 crates), cargo clippy (4 real -D warnings violations), cargo test (2 rustls feature-unification failures), and the 250 pure-LOC ceiling (20 production modules over limit, worst 1304). SPDX presence and bench-schema gates pass. The nix-toolchain clippy E0514, missing BPF/PostgreSQL/SPIRE/OIDC infrastructure, and the spdx-lint allowlist string-mismatch are documented but NOT counted as quality failures per task guidance. To reach APPROVE: (1) reconcile rustfmt toolchain/config and reformat; (2) fix the 4 clippy lints; (3) resolve rustls crypto-provider feature unification in identity-spiffe; (4) split oversized modules (starting with policy-rollout/state_machine.rs) or baseline them with due-dates; (5) optionally fix the spdx-lint allowlist and the rules/lists.rs:109 bare unwrap.
